reserveReview.reviewer: Sol curation pass 2026-10-01 (FixInv6); fallback composition re-curated from the August 2026 USDtb examination, Schedule II

sources.label: USDtb Reserve Report - August 2026 (Deloitte via Anchorage)

reserveReview.rationale: The independently examined August 31, 2026 fallback composition is BUIDL at fair value $525,205,527 (99.017%) and cash $5,214,126 (0.983%) out of $530,419,653 reserve assets, supporting $529,269,213 redeemable USDtb. Schedule II identifies all cash as directly held U.S. demand deposits at FDIC-insured depository institutions, with $4,964,126 above the FDIC limit. BUIDL is self-custodied in segregated wallets on Solana ($223,271,995), BSC ($111,095,606), Avalanche ($45,754,629), and Aptos ($145,083,297). Percentages are calculated from the reported reserve-asset total and rounded to four decimal places. The existing adapter-owned source keys remain unchanged; these rows are the dated examined fallback, not an assertion that the rolling live endpoint has the same weights. The composition date matches proofOfReserves.latestReport.periodEnd.
reserveReview.compositionBasis: Deloitte & Touche LLP examination of the USDtb Reserve Report as of August 31, 2026, Schedule II asset-type balances divided by total reserve assets, mapped onto the usdtb-transparency adapter's two existing slice identities
reserveReview.knownUnknownExposure: All examined reserve assets are classified (BUIDL fund shares at fair value; FDIC-insured bank demand deposits). Individual deposit bank names are not disclosed, and BUIDL's own underlying fund holdings are governed by BlackRock's separate fund disclosures rather than this examination.

custodyProfile.uncertainty: Anchorage reports that BUIDL is self-custodied in segregated wallets and cash is held in segregated fiduciary trust accounts at unnamed major commercial banks. D10 review on 2026-10-01: the May and August examinations describe unencumbered reserves only at their report dates, while the covered stablecoin terms impose prudent trust investment and management obligations without an express standing permission or prohibition on rehypothecation. The prior 2026-07-14 prohibited classification is withdrawn as unsupported policy evidence and retained in the curation history. Investment through BUIDL remains distinct from legal reuse rights; current allocations and insolvency treatment have not been independently adjudicated.
